clinician.trajectory_summary: An 80-year-old man presented with a 3-month history of frontal headaches and bilateral jaw claudication. Initial CT head was negative for masses but showed an incidental lacunar infarct. Ophthalmology history revealed episodes of diplopia, amaurosis fugax, and significant weight loss without fever or scalp tenderness. Physical exam found bilateral tender, nodular and weakly pulsatile temporal arteries. Inflammatory markers (CRP and ESR) were not significantly elevated. Temporal and axillary artery ultrasound demonstrated a characteristic positive halo sign in the right temporal artery. A right temporal artery biopsy showed a muscular artery with focal adventitial chronic inflammation and intimal hyperplasia with mild inflammation, consistent with GCA.
